gap: No result ChatGPT got says what its cycle count means: the Dakota Powerbox 10 pages (2,000+) and the Bixpower LF1220 pages (2000 Times) give neither the depth of discharge nor the capacity left at end of life, so neither can be set against makers that rate cycles at 100% DoD.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages. invertersrus.com (Dakota Powerbox 10) gives '2,000+ recharge cycles' with no DoD or end-of-life capacity. tackledirect.com (same product) gives no cycle figure. bixpower.com has two pages, the LF1220 and the LF1220 + 60 W solar kit. Both say '2000 Times' with no conditions, though the LF1220 page does say the battery 'can safely discharge to ~20%'. All of these pages already give charger amps and continuous and peak current, so those columns are not new. What is new is that the cycle counts have no conditions. But I could not open a maker page that gives the conditioned figure to compare against: Redodo, Power Queen, ECO-WORTHY and the Dakota maker pages all returned HTTP 429, and the Power Queen fetch also failed on a TLS error. So the normalised table is only half sourced, and the finding does not yet decide the pick.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick, for now. The small kits ChatGPT found (Dakota 10 Ah with a 3 A charger, Bixpower 20 Ah with a 6 A charger) all charge at the same 0.3C, about 3.3 h on paper. So they differ on cycle rating and price, not on charging. Their '2,000' cycle figures have no conditions, so the page must not rank them against the 100 Ah kits on cycle count until Redodo, Power Queen or ECO-WORTHY state their conditions (DoD, C-rate, end capacity) on a page we have actually opened. If the Redodo figure of 4,000 cycles at 100% DoD, 0.2C and 25 °C checks out on the maker page, the footnote becomes: 'a bare 2,000 is not half of 4,000 at 100% DoD; the two cannot be compared'.
